system_prompt:
You are an MLB contract prediction agent. Given a player and a target season, predict the contract they would sign (or the salary they would be paid) for that season.

You currently have NO tools: rely on your own knowledge of MLB players, salaries, the CBA, and market history. Acknowledge uncertainty honestly — if you are unsure who a player is or how they have performed recently, say so in your reasoning and lower your confidence.

CONTRACT PHASES (provided in the request — do not re-derive it):
- pre-arb: fewer than 3 years of MLB service. Salaries cluster tightly at the CBA league
  minimum (roughly $0.70M-0.78M in 2022-2026, rising ~$30K/year), occasionally slightly above.
  Duration is always 1 year.
- arb: 3-6 years of service. Salary set by the arbitration system: driven by service year
  (arb-1/2/3), counting stats, and raises over the prior salary. Duration is 1 year.
- free-agent: open-market deal. AAV and duration are driven by recent performance, age,
  position, and market comparables. Multi-year contracts are common.

OUTPUT RULES:
- All dollar values are in MILLIONS of USD (e.g. league minimum 2024 = 0.74).
- total_value_millions must equal aav_millions * duration_years.
- aav_low_millions / aav_high_millions bound the plausible AAV range.

CITATIONS (required):
- Every material figure in your prediction (salary anchors, league minimum values,
  comparable contracts, performance claims) must be supported by a citation.
- Use source_type="model_knowledge" with:
  - claim: the specific figure or fact (e.g. "league minimum was $0.74M in 2024")
  - basis: what you know it from and how current that knowledge is
    (e.g. "2022-2026 CBA minimum salary schedule").
- If a figure is an estimate rather than a remembered fact, say so in the basis.
- Your knowledge has a training cutoff: state in your reasoning when the target season
  is beyond what you have reliable knowledge of.

Predict the 2026 contract for this player:

Player: Tyrone Taylor (Taylor_28137)
Position: CF
Target season: 2026
Contract phase: arb (resolved deterministically, method=observed)
Estimated MLB service time entering 2026: 5.54 years
Estimated age in 2026: 32

Respond with your structured prediction, citing every material figure.

content.text:
Predict the 2026 contract for this player:

Player: Tyrone Taylor (Taylor_28137)
Position: CF
Target season: 2026
Contract phase: arb (resolved deterministically, method=observed)
Estimated MLB service time entering 2026: 5.54 years
Estimated age in 2026: 32

Respond with your structured prediction, citing every material figure.

input.reasoning: Tyrone Taylor enters 2026 with ~5.5 MLB years (user-provided) so he is arbitration-eligible and in the 3–6 year arbitration window; arbitration awards are one-year. Given his profile (veteran fourth/fifth-year regular/role CF without top-tier offensive production) and typical arbitration outcomes for 5–6 year players through my 2024 knowledge cutoff, a mid-single-million one-year arbitration award is the most likely outcome. I estimate $3.8M for 2026 (one year). Range $2.0–6.0M captures lower-end outcomes if counting stats decline or he settles for a modest raise, and higher-end outcomes if he posts an unusually strong counting year or wins a favorable arbitration decision. I am moderately uncertain because I do not have Taylor’s exact 2024–25 counting stats or recent arbitration hearing comparables past my 2024 cutoff.

citations.claim: Arbitration covers players with 3–6 years of MLB service and arbitration awards are settled as one-year contracts.
citations.basis: Standard MLB service-time/arbitration structure from the collective bargaining agreement and common baseball knowledge up through my 2024 training cutoff (players with 3–6 years are arbitration-eligible; arbitration salaries are one-year).

citations.claim: User-provided estimated MLB service time entering 2026 = 5.54 years and estimated age in 2026 = 32.
citations.basis: These service-time and age figures were supplied in the prompt and used as the basis for determining arbitration phase and estimating market value.

citations.claim: A mid-single-million arbitration award (~$2–6M) is a common range for 5–6 year players without star-level production.
citations.basis: Observed arbitration awards and settlements through 2024 show many 4–6 year players with modest counting stats receiving mid-single-million salaries; I am using that historical pattern and comparable-arbitration outcomes as the basis for the estimate (knowledge cutoff June 2024).

citations.claim: Predicted 2026 one-year arbitration salary for Tyrone Taylor: $3.8M (AAV) — total value $3.8M for one year; plausible range $2.0–6.0M.
citations.basis: Estimate derived from Taylor’s arbitration phase (5.54 years), positional role (center field), age (32), and my knowledge of arbitration settlements up to 2024; exact figure is an informed estimate because I lack Taylor’s 2024–25 performance data beyond my 2024 cutoff.
